title: PHOTO-FENTON TREATMENT OF PHARMACEUTICAL MICROPOLLUTANTS IN TREATED MUNICIPAL WASTEWATER: BOX–BEHNKEN OPTIMIZATION

PHOTO-FENTON TREATMENT OF PHARMACEUTICAL MICROPOLLUTANTS IN TREATED MUNICIPAL WASTEWATER: BOX–BEHNKEN OPTIMIZATION

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Hassan Alzoubi, Salah H. Aljbour, Husam Al-Hamaiedh, Tayel El-Hasan, Hadeel Hosney, Eldon R. Rene

ABSTRACT

Water scarcity is a major environmental problem worldwide and is particularly severe in dry regions such as Jordan. The presence of pharmaceutical residues in treated wastewater limits its safe reuse and poses risks to human health and the environment. This study evaluated the Photo-Fenton process for removing six pharmaceutical compounds, namely azithromycin, bisoprolol, diazinon, diclofenac, ibuprofen, and ketoconazole, from secondary-treated municipal wastewater collected from the Wadi Al-Shallalah Wastewater Treatment Plant in Jordan. A four-factor Box-Behnken design (27 runs) was used to study the effects of pH, temperature, Fe2+ concentration, and H2O2 dosage on the removal efficiency, and the fitted models were evaluated by analysis of variance (ANOVA) including a lack-of-fit test. Temperature was the only statistically significant main effect for all six compounds, whereas Fe2+ acted mainly through a significant quadratic (curvature) term; pH and H2O2 dosage had secondary effects within the tested ranges. The highest removal efficiencies, ranging from about 80% to 90%, were obtained at 30 °C, pH 3.0, Fe2+ 5 mg/L, and H2O2 50 mg/L. The results show that the Photo-Fenton process can serve as an effective polishing (tertiary) step for pharmaceutical removal from municipal wastewater and provides a scalable option for improving effluent quality under Jordanian conditions.
